blocks.text:
After breakfast, you will travel by motorcycle to the park, where the hike begins. The trail crosses gentle savannah hills and shallow rivers on the way to Parai Tepuy, a Pemón village. Along the way you can see Roraima Tepui and Kukenán Tepui.

The main trek begins after lunch. First you cross the Tek River, then you reach the Kukenán River. During the rainy season, from June to December, water levels can be high and the current strong. In those conditions, you wade across with the aid of a rope.

The trail then climbs through the valley to the foot of Roraima. You camp in tents in the lowlands, where tropical birds and fireflies can be found. Just before camp, you can see the tepui’s vast quartz wall.

**Meals:** breakfast, packed lunch, dinner.

blocks.text: Thursday: Ascent to the Roraima Plateau

Early morning after breakfast, continue along the only available diagonal route across the base of Mount Roraima. The narrow trail winds through mountain rainforests with small streams and rivers. Near the mountain base, the colorful vegetation transitions to shrubs, highland mosses, and ferns among rocks.

The trail leads to the “Two Tears” waterfall and then to the “living stones”, where careful attention is needed. Reach the summit of Roraima and continue toward the massive rock formations. Weather on the tepui summit is unpredictable, with sudden storms and heavy clouds possible at any time of year. Set up camp, have dinner, and celebrate reaching the top. Overnight in tents.

Meals: breakfast, lunch (packed), dinner
